title: Tempered escalation policy and noise mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Recent capacity regressions and two SLO breaches in Q1 revealed that our current pagering model produces high-frequency noisy pages for low-impact burst events and cascades during autoscaler oscillations. This ticket proposes a tempered escalation policy (a short-term quarantine window + graded escalation thresholds) combined with a noise-mitigation playbook to reduce fatigue while preserving response for genuine outages.

Goals:
- Reduce operational pagers from these classes of events by at least 60% without increasing time-to-detect for high-severity incidents.
- Add automated context-aware quarantine for burn-rate alerts that filters transient spikes shorter than 90s unless corroborated by supporting signals.
- Provide on-call UX changes: clearer alert summaries, fast-silence options for recurring known issues, and a rollback path for mis-suppression.

Proposed design:
1) Quarantine window: for burn-rate alerts that originate from a single region/pool, introduce a 60-90s probation window where the platform records the event but suppresses immediate paging. If within that window either request-error-rate or instance-count-change crosses a corroborating threshold, escalate immediately.
2) Graded escalation: classify alerts into Informational / Operational / Outage tiers. Only Operational+ tier pages by default; Informational notifications go to Slack/console. Tiers are computed by weighted impact: error-rate, affected-rps, customer-affinity, and model-tier (hosted vs dedicated).
3) Spike decay: apply a short half-life decay to burn-rate signals so short single-sample spikes do not immediately trigger burn alarms.
4) Incident quarantine override: provide a one-click on-call override to force immediate paging in a quarantine window; this will be logged for post-incident review.
5) Rollout: start with canary for non-prod and the developer sandbox (testbed) for 2 weeks, then enable for P0 and P1 customers on Hosted, followed by Dedicated after telemetry validation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic tests that generate transient spikes show >=60% reduction in pages while simulated sustained regressions still page 100% of the time.
- Metrics dashboard panels for "Quarantine suppressions", "Missed-pages false-negative rate", and "Time-to-first-action by tier" created in Console.
- Runbook updated and playbook published in Confluence with examples and rollback steps.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Excessive suppression could hide real outages. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, immediate escalation if supporting signals present, and mandatory audit logs for suppressed events.
- Risk: Complexity for on-call. Mitigation: UI improvements (fast-snooze, explicit suppression reason), training session for SRE team, and staged rollout.
